official_measurement_examples.name: Current statutory minimum
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG's July 2026 Healthy Homes publication identifies Part M Category 1 M4(1) as the statutory minimum for new homes, while higher M4(2) and M4(3) provision depends on adopted local planning policy.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three dwelling categories
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document M Volume 1 distinguishes Category 1 visitable dwellings, Category 2 accessible and adaptable dwellings, and Category 3 wheelchair user dwellings.

official_measurement_examples.name: Optional requirement trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document M states M4(2) and M4(3) apply only where required by planning permission under the optional-requirements framework.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2022 policy intention
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2022 government response proposed mandating M4(2) as the minimum for new homes but said implementation required further Building Regulations and Approved Document changes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning evidence test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Housing optional technical standards guidance says local planning authorities should evidence need for M4(2) and M4(3) and consider viability and site circumstances.

official_measurement_examples.name: Non-lift serviced flats
official_measurement_examples.fact: PPG says where step-free access in non-lift serviced multi-storey development is not viable, M4(2) and M4(3) optional requirements should not be applied.

official_measurement_examples.name: Changing Places amendment
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2020 Volume 2 amendment introduced Changing Places toilet guidance for specified new publicly accessible buildings.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2015 regulatory basis
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2015 amendment regulations introduced optional access requirements that apply when compliance is made a condition of planning permission.

core_rules: Approved Document M compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Building Regulations compliance
M4(1) is distinct from M4(2)
M4(2) is distinct from M4(3)
M4(2) optional requirement is not automatically applicable nationally
M4(3) optional requirement is not automatically applicable nationally
planning policy requirement must be evidenced for the actual authority and site
adopted local policy is distinct from draft accessibility policy
M4 category is not parcel housing capacity
M4 category is not dwelling ownership evidence
M4(2) planning trigger is not Building Regulations approval
M4(3) planning trigger is not Building Regulations approval
2022 government response is not itself an amended Building Regulation
proposal to mandate M4(2) must not be treated as implemented without later legal evidence
July 2026 Healthy Homes core requirement is not a statutory replacement for current Part M unless legislation says so
Healthy Homes good practice is distinct from statutory minimum
M4(1) visitable standard is not proof a completed dwelling complies
M4(2) accessible and adaptable label requires actual design compliance evidence
M4(3) wheelchair user label requires actual design compliance evidence
M4(3) wheelchair adaptable and wheelchair accessible subtypes must not be conflated
step-free access requirement is not planning permission
step-free access infeasibility is not automatic planning refusal
non-lift serviced flat exception is site-specific not a national exemption
local need evidence is not site allocation
viability assessment is not Building Regulations approval
planning condition requiring M4(2) must be read from the actual decision
planning condition requiring M4(3) must be read from the actual decision
absence of an M4 condition is not proof M4(1) compliance
Building Control acceptance is not planning permission
completion certificate is not planning permission
Changing Places toilet requirement is not a dwelling M4(3) requirement
Changing Places guidance applies only to its defined building scope
Volume 1 dwelling guidance is distinct from Volume 2 non-dwelling guidance
2024 Volume 2 amendment must not be back-applied without transition evidence
historic 2015 edition must retain its amendment state
2016 correction is not a new planning policy
accessible route geometry is not a Land Registry boundary
parking provision under M4 does not prove highway access
private outdoor-space accessibility is not land ownership
wheelchair turning space is not dwelling floor-area planning capacity
accessible sanitary provision is not HMO licensing compliance
Part M compliance is distinct from Equality Act duties
Equality Act duty is not planning permission
planning policy evidence is distinct from individual Building Regulations inspection
source edition and effective dates must be preserved
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no accessibility constraint
no parcel accessibility compliance housing capacity or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research confidence is not parcel Part M accuracy
